items.stem: A type error appears in a generated React component. Claude Code proposes casting the value to any. The better fix is to:

options.text: Model the correct type so the error reflects real data instead of being suppressed
options.rationale: Correct: precise types catch real mismatches; any discards that safety.

options.text: Cast to any to move on quickly
options.rationale: any removes type safety and hides real mismatches.
Disabling checks defeats the purpose of using TypeScript.
Deleting working UI is not a fix for a type error.

items.explanation: Correct: precise types catch real mismatches; any discards that safety.

items.stem: Which TWO checks help verify a React/TypeScript change before shipping? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The type-checker passes with no new errors
options.rationale: Correct: a clean type-check is a baseline front-end gate.

options.text: The running app shows no new console errors
options.rationale: Correct: runtime console errors reveal problems a build may not.

options.text: The component file has more lines than before
options.rationale: Line count is not a correctness signal.
A rename is unrelated to verifying the change.

items.explanation: Correct: a clean type-check is a baseline front-end gate.

items.stem: A list shows a stale value after an update. The most likely cause to investigate first is:

options.text: A missing or incorrect effect/hook dependency
options.rationale: Correct: stale values commonly stem from dependency-array mistakes.
Offline status would usually surface differently, not as a stale render.
Compiler version rarely causes a stale rendered value.
File length does not cause stale state.
